column2: Reconstruction of the Garabagh Irrigation Canal
column3: Project objective is to improve agricultural productivity, reduce irrigation water losses, and contribute to rural development and livelihoods in line with “Azerbaijan 2030” Vision, aiming for green growth, climate resilience, and food security. column2: Inter-Island Connectivity Project
column3: The Project is focused on improving maritime transport connectivity, resilience and safety between the islands, supporting economic integration in Comoros. Comoros has various untapped growth potentials, but such potential areas remain fragmented because of poor transport connectivity among and within the islands. Poverty is persistently high particularly in remote areas, with regional inequality widening. In addition, Comoros is highly vulnerable to climatic events and natural hazards, such as tropical cyclones, high waves and coastal flooding. Maritime transport safety is becoming a particular concern for local users. The Project addresses efficiency, reliability and safety in both formal and informal (called kwassa kwassa) maritime transport sectors.The main project objectives are: - Increased economic resilience by facilitating economic internal exchanges between island as well as external exchanges.- Reduce disparities in transport infrastructure and improve social well-being.- Induce increased demand.- Reduce the cost of transportation for people and goods;- Reduce travel time; - Ensure the safety of maritime transport users.

column2: Enhancing the Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) Contribution to the Food Security in Egypt Project
column3: The overall goal of the project is to contribute to strengthening the food security of Egypt by enhancing the productivity and sustainability of MSEs operating in the food and agriculture sector. A total of 1,100 MSEs operating in the food and agriculture sector, with 20% being women-owned and 20% being youth-owned enterprises, will have access to Shariah-compliant financing. Various agricultural production activities, along with their value chains including food processing, packing, and marketing will be supported. In addition, the trading of wholesale or retail of food products and agricultural inputs, including agricultural and irrigation equipment, will be part of the financing. Furthermore, nearly 600 stakeholders including MSEs owners and MSMEDA staff will be provided a training on Islamic Finance. At the end of the project, around one million people will have access to food security products in the targeted area. Furthermore, the MSEs will generate 2,900 new employment opportunities, with a special emphasis on rural areas, women and youth. Additionally, as a result of this project, the Islamic Finance window in MSMEDA operations will experience a significant increase from 1.6% to 3.5%.

column2: Enhancing the Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) Contribution to the Food Security in Egypt Project
column3: The overall goal of the project is to contribute to strengthening the food security of Egypt by enhancing the productivity and sustainability of MSEs operating in the food and agriculture sector. A total of 1,100 MSEs operating in the food and agriculture sector, with 20% being women-owned and 20% being youth-owned enterprises, will have access to Shariah-compliant financing. Various agricultural production activities, along with their value chains including food processing, packing, and marketing will be supported. In addition, the trading of wholesale or retail of food products and agricultural inputs, including agricultural and irrigation equipment, will be part of the financing. Furthermore, nearly 600 stakeholders including MSEs owners and MSMEDA staff will be provided a training on Islamic Finance. At the end of the project, around one million people will have access to food security products in the targeted area. Furthermore, the MSEs will generate 2,900 new employment opportunities, with a special emphasis on rural areas, women and youth. Additionally, as a result of this project, the Islamic Finance window in MSMEDA operations will experience a significant increase from 1.6% to 3.5%.
